top.description: For a while it was the NES . I’d shoot ducks until I got bored, and I hated Mario because it was too hard. What I really remember fondly was watching Mémère play The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past after she upgraded to the SNES. She’d tell me who she was fighting and why, and following along felt like having one of my favorite people read me a book. When it was my turn to play, I’d just charge up Link’s sword and mow every blade of grass I could find. Then I’d go looking for chickens. Then I’d ask what she had for snacks. She always had good snacks for me.

top.title: Senate passes bill to reform senior secondary education
top.description: By Henry Umoru The Senate has passed the National Senior Secondary Education Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeking to strengthen the administration, coordination and governance of public senior secondary education in Nigeria. The executive bill, sponsored by President Bola Tinubu, was transmitted to the Senate in July 2026 for legislative consideration. The proposed legislation, titled the National Senior Secondary Education Commission Act (Amendment) Bill, 2026 (SB. 1075), was passed on Wednesday after consideration of the report of the Senate Committee on Education (Basic and Secondary). Senator Orji Uzor Kalu (APC, Abia North) presented the committee’s report on behalf of its chairman, Senator Lawal Adamu Usman (Kaduna Central). Following a clause-by-clause consideration of the report at the Committee of the Whole, the Senate approved the bill, which was subsequently read for the third time and passed. Presenting the report, Kalu urged the Senate to consider and adopt the recommendations of the committee on the proposed legislation. According to the report, the National Senior Secondary Education Commission was established under the National Senior Secondary Education Commission Act, 2023, to regulate and promote the development of senior secondary education in Nigeria. It stated that experience gained in implementing the Act had revealed areas requiring amendments to strengthen governance, improve coordination between the Federal and State Governments, promote accountability and support the effective implementation of national education policies. The report added that the proposed amendments were intended to address the identified challenges and make the legislation more effective in achieving its objectives. Kalu disclosed that the House of Representatives had also considered the bill and referred it to its Committee on Basic Education and Services for further legislative action. He said this informed the decision to conduct a joint stakeholder hearing and clause-by-clause consideration to ensure comprehensive consolidation, a uniform report and smoother legislative proceedings. Recall that President Tinubu transmitted the executive bill to the Senate in July through a letter read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio during plenary. In the letter, Tinubu said the Federal Executive Council had approved the amendment bill at its meeting on April 30, 2026, before the Federal Ministry of Justice vetted and finalised it in line with constitutional provisions and legislative drafting standards. The President said the proposed amendment was part of his administration’s commitment to strengthening educational institutions in the national interest. Following the presentation of the bill, Akpabio referred it to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for legislative processing and directed it to report back within one week. top.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has restricted the right to speak on its behalf to three persons, ordering that everyone previously announced in that role be dissolved into the Directorate of Media and Strategic Communications as members. The Chief of Staff to the President and Deputy Director-General (Administration) of the Council, Femi Gbajabiamila, announced the changes in a statement issued on Wednesday, titled “Reorganization of Media and Communications Structure”. top.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
top.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. top.title: 2027: Obi is desperate, not wired for long-term solutions — Oshiomhole
top.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Senator Adams Oshiomhole has accused Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi of focusing on importation rather than job creation and long-term solutions, alleging that his promise to serve only four years reflects desperation to become president. Oshiomhole made the remarks while campaigning for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Akure, the Ondo State capital, on Wednesday. Framing the 2027 election as a choice about Nigeria’s future, he urged young voters to back Tinubu and contrasted what he described as the President’s long-term development agenda and plans to improve the power sector with Obi’s business record and four-year pledge. Addressing young Nigerians, the APC chieftain urged students, graduates and young workers to compare the time it takes industrialists such as Aliko Dangote to establish factories and create jobs with what he described as Obi’s focus on setting up shopping malls. “That said, I need to talk to us, you young people. What this election is about is you. You as students, some of you are graduates, some of you are young workers. You talk to Dangote and ask him how long does it take him to set up a factory, to set up a refinery that today employs 10s of 1000s of workers. Then go and ask Obi how long it takes him to set up a shopping mall. To set up a shopping mall, you need short-term funds, and that is the logic of Peter Obi,” he said. Oshiomhole alleged that Obi was not inclined to develop long-term solutions that could produce sustainable growth. He also questioned Obi’s business record, asking why an unemployed person should accept advice on job creation from someone he accused of selling imported products instead of locally made Yoruba Adire. “He cannot; he’s not wired to think of long-term solutions that produce sustainable growth and development. Another one: if there is anybody who is unemployed, ask Obi, why are you selling imported products?” Oshiomhole asked. He further argued that a person whose main business was importation could not credibly lecture Nigerians on job creation, and described Obi’s pledge to serve for four years as evidence of what he called desperation. “So, anyone whose main business is importation cannot lecture us about job creation because he doesn’t mean it. Turning to Tinubu’s re-election bid, Oshiomhole said the President knew the need to increase the purchasing power of poorer Nigerians and create jobs. Since then, the 49-year-old golfer has faced several personal and physical challenges, including recovering from a ruptured Achilles tendon and his seventh back surgery. top.title: Allofs brothers see their history reflected on El Mala duo
top.description: FILE PHOTO - Cologne's Said El Mala (L) and his brother Malek El Mala are picture after the German Bundesliga soccer match betweem 1.FC Cologne and Bayer Leverkusen at RheinEnergieStadion. (is associated with: «Allofs brothers see their history reflected on El Mala duo») Rolf Vennenbernd/dpa Two brothers, one club and a special connection: Klaus and Thomas Allofs see a piece of their own football history reflected in Said and Malek El Mala. Like the El Mala brothers, the Allofs once played together for Cologne. "A pair of brothers like that is something special, it makes the whole story even more emotionally rich," Klaus Allofs told broadcaster Sport1 in an interview. "When the goal was scored, the connection to us was immediately there. I even think that my wife said: 'Look, just like you two back then,'" Klaus Allofs said. He was referring to Said El Mala's goal in the 2-1 defeat to Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday, which was assisted by his brother Malek. His brother Thomas received a photo of the two sets of brothers from friends and acquaintances. "That's when I really realized how extraordinary it is that two brothers play together as strikers in a Bundesliga team," said Klaus Allofs. Forty years ago, the Allofs brothers played together for Cologne. Now, Said and Malek El Mala are making waves in the city. Klaus Allofs is particularly impressed with the younger, Said, who has already made his debut for the Germany national team. "He's an exceptional player," said the former Germany international. "Based on his pure potential, he belongs in the top tier." However, Thomas Allofs sees some challenges for both players. "The pressure on Said and also on Malek is huge. The difficulty is to consistently deliver a good performance," he said. Furthermore, Thomas Allofs believes that constant comparisons between the brothers could also become a burden within a family. Klaus added: "Right now, of course, everything is wonderful. But there will be phases for both of them when things don't go so well."

top.description: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images The Texas Rangers are ready to listen to offers for shortstop Corey Seager as General Manager meetings start Wednesday in Las Vegas. According to Fox Sports ‘ Ken Rosenthal, the front office expects to hear what other clubs will give up for the star player. The move comes from a team that won the World Series last year.d Series in 2023. Seager carries a massive contract and a no-trade clause, but his value on the field has dropped due to injuries. The Rangers know they must act now before the new Collective Bargaining Agreement changes the rules of the game. The Money Problem Is Real The team’s financial constraints make completing the deal before the season starts difficult. Over the next five years of Seager’s 10-year, $325 million contract, he is owed $155 million. That huge number scares off teams that do not want to take on such a heavy payroll impact. Fox Sports reported that owners are pushing for a salary cap system, which makes other clubs hesitant to absorb that cost. Even with his no-trade clause, the two sides could try to find a fit that works for the player and the club. Health Issues Keep Him on the Sidelines Seager has found it difficult to remain on the field since agreeing to his major contract with the Rangers. He missed time in 2023 with hamstring and thumb issues, then faced sports hernia and hip procedures in 2024. He has not played 150 games in a single season since 2022. His production slipped last year when he played just 102 games and hit only .227. The Rangers need a reliable shortstop, and Seager’s health history includes injuries that could affect his long‑term availability. Yet his elite production when healthy is undeniable and still draws interest from other teams. A Wait-and-See Market Ahead The CBA expires on December 1, and a lockout could stop all deals until owners and players agree on new terms. This uncertainty means the majority of free-agent signings and trades might wait until the new deal is reached. In 12 seasons, he posted a .284 batting average, 241 home runs, 718 RBIs and a 46.3 WAR. The Rangers will explore the market, but a deal depends on finding a team willing to take the risk.

top.title: Deutsche Bank Switches On Bitcoin Custody for Paying Clients
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine Deutsche Bank Switches On Bitcoin Custody for Paying Clients Deutsche Bank has switched on its digital asset custody service for paying clients, the German lender said Wednesday, letting institutions and corporations in Europe hold bitcoin with the country’s largest bank less than two months after it first unveiled the plan. The bank announced the service on Sept. 16, saying it would go live with first clients this year once regulators signed off. It now supports bitcoin and ether, along with the USDC, EURC and EURAU stablecoins, according to its product page . Under the setup, Deutsche Bank manages the wallets and private keys on behalf of clients, who can store the assets and transfer them to third parties. The bank pitched that as a way for clients to skip building and maintaining their own custody infrastructure. “In the medium term we aim to deliver a fully integrated, regulated ecosystem that supports the custody, tokenisation, and settlement of digital assets,” said Paul Maley, global head of trust and securities services at Deutsche Bank. The bank did not name its first clients, say how many have signed up or disclose what it charges to hold the coins. The service is aimed at institutional and corporate clients, not retail customers. What Deutsche Bank is offering The product page describes private keys stored in hardware security modules, a choice of warm and cold storage, multi-factor authentication, segregation of client assets and a customizable approval process for client transfers. Clients reach the service through Autobahn, Deutsche Bank’s multi-channel gateway, or its Corporate Bank portal. The service is booked out of Deutsche Bank AG in Frankfurt and is available in Germany, with cross-border servicing across Europe through passporting. The bank lists institutional investors, multinationals and corporates, governments and sovereigns, and wealth managers as target clients, and it describes the offering as compliant with the European Union’s MiCA crypto rules. For now the menu is narrow. Deutsche lists custody, transfers and internal moves between warm and cold storage as its initial services, with “further capabilities planned.” The September release said the asset list may grow with client demand and that tokenized financial instruments are on the roadmap. It also carried a warning familiar to anyone in bitcoin: crypto assets held this way are not covered by a deposit-guarantee scheme like the one that protects eligible bank deposits. A tie-up with Deutsche Asset Management Alongside the launch, Deutsche Bank signed a memorandum of understanding with Deutsche Asset Management, the money manager it mostly owns that was known until recently as DWS. The agreement is meant “to explore comprehensive commercial and technical collaboration opportunities in the digital asset space,” the bank said. top.title: Zidane hands Eli Junior Kroupi first France call-up as Marcus Thuram and Aurélien Tchouaméni withdraw injured
top.description: Zidane hands Eli Junior Kroupi first France call-up as Marcus Thuram and Aurélien Tchouaméni withdraw injured Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi has been called up to the senior France squad for the first time after Marcus Thuram and Aurélien Tchouaméni both withdrew with injuries. Zinedine Zidane turned to the uncapped striker as a replacement for Thuram, who has been ruled out of France's UEFA Nations League fixtures with a hamstring problem. Thuram picked up the injury on Sunday in Inter's 2-0 Serie A win over Como, a game in which he scored the second goal. Persistent discomfort kept him out of Monday's training session, and he remained under the care of the medical staff. "With no improvement this morning, and following medical examinations, the French national team's medical staff decided, in agreement with Inter and the player, to release him back to his club," France said in a statement on Tuesday . Tchouaméni is also heading home. The Real Madrid midfielder aggravated his right adductor in training, the same injury he suffered at the World Cup in the summer, and will return to Madrid for rehabilitation. Zidane will not call up a replacement for him. Kroupi's route into the squad Kroupi finished as Ligue 2's top scorer in 2025 and was part of the France Under-19 side that reached the final of the 2024 European Championship, finishing as runners-up. The 20-year-old has rejected past advances from Portugal, given his desire to represent France at senior level. He's also eligible to represent Ivory Coast. Kroupi's call-up follows a disrupted start to the campaign. The forward injured his foot during Bournemouth's preseason training camp and needed surgery, only returning to action for the club last month. However, his performances last season have impressed the French set-up. Kroupi scored 13 league goals during his debut Premier League season, a record for a teenager in their first season in the division. Zidane's growing injury list Thuram and Tchouaméni are the latest names on a lengthy list of absentees. Juventus defender Pierre Kalulu has already been ruled out with a left hamstring injury, with uncapped right-back Saël Kumbedi drafted in to replace him. Despite the absences, France lead their Nations League group with 10 points from four games. Zidane's side travel to Italy on Thursday before hosting Türkiye three days later.

top.title: England cancel Windies Test in favour of home Ashes warm-ups
top.description: Sophie Ecclestone has taken five-wicket hauls in her last two Tests [Getty Images] England have cancelled their scheduled Test in the West Indies in April and will instead prepare for the Women's Ashes with a number of red-ball matches in the UK. Nat Sciver-Brunt's side have played just one Test - a heavy defeat by India at Lord's - since their last four-day meeting with Australia in January 2025, which they lost by an innings in Melbourne. Next summer's Test against Australia, which is worth four points in the multi-format series, will be held at Headingley from 24-27 June. England will prepare for that with four red-ball matches. One of the games will be a three-day fixture against Australia A before three intra-squad 'best v best' matches. In addition, a dedicated red-ball training camp will be held in Bangalore in January. England expect to use 26 or 27 players across the different training camps and matches. It means England's schedule in the West Indies has been revised to three T20s and three one-day internationals only. The change comes after it was suggested the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) might need to offer financial support to Cricket West Indies (CWI) to allow the Test to take place. "We would welcome any assistance of our much wealthier member boards," CWI chief executive Chris Dehring previously told BBC Sport. "It is very expensive to host cricket in the Caribbean." However, BBC Sport understands the ECB's decision is not related to those financial discussions and the schedule change is viewed as a performance decision in line with giving England the best chance of winning the Ashes. West Indies have not played a women's Test since 2004, which was their only red-ball match in 47 years. "A 10-day warm-weather red-ball camp in India followed by four further matches in English conditions will provide Charlotte Edwards and her team with the appropriate game time to be ready for that challenge [of Australia]," said ECB chief executive Richard Gould. "Best versus best in English conditions provides a valuable opportunity for the team. "It also allows us to assess our strength in depth, give opportunities to more players and get a number of competitive multi-day cricket matches across a longer period into the wider group." top.title: Michigan State's ferocious defense is its 'best brand of basketball'
top.description: CHICAGO – As Jordan Scott elevated for his sixth and most important block of the night, Dame Sarr turned and watch the ball he shot flying into the expensive seats next to Duke’s bench. Scott came down from the stratosphere of United Center and landed with a guttural yell. Jasiah Jervis gave him a chest-bump, and the rest of his Michigan State teammates hustled over to dap him up, as well. “I might’ve jumped higher than Coen [Carr] over there,” Scott said later with a grin and a laugh. In one swooping moment, and throughout a thorough 79-73 victory over No. 2 Duke in the Champions Classic , the fifth-ranked Spartans delivered a sweeping statement to the Blue Devils and the rest of the college basketball world. "What is that, six blocks to match his jersey number?" Watch each Jordan Scott's career-high six blocks in No. 5 @MSU_Basketball 's win against No. 2 Duke 👇 pic.twitter.com/xhkyRyReBc — Big Ten Men's Basketball (@B1GMBBall) November 11, 2026 And their defense and toughness were their calling cards. “We knew that they were a tough team, they were a physical team,” said point guard Jeremy Fears Jr., who had 18 points, 11 assists, seven rebounds, a steal and a block. “And at the same time, we knew that we had a chance with the game in our hands. Our goal is to always play physical, play tough. … So we just wanted to play our best brand of basketball, and hopefully that led to something good.” MSU (3-0) had eight blocked shots as a team and seven steals among 13 forced turnovers, scoring 16 points off of those takeaways. The Spartans never trailed and held Duke (2-1) to just 33.3% shooting overall and 7-for-29 from 3-point range. It was the type of blue-collar a performance against a blueblood that makes Tom Izzo a happy coach – “I did think we played with a little more toughness” – even though he admitted it still is only three games into the season and merely an in-the-moment measuring stick. But also a proud program moment for Izzo, who is now 4-15 all-time against the Blue Devils and 2-4 against them in the Champions Classic. “Now, they deserve what they've gotten against us, but we haven't taken a backseat to anybody, either,” Izzo said. “And I don't plan on taking a backseat in the near future or in the far future, to be honest with you.” The Spartans asserted their dominance early, staggering Duke off the tip with an 11-2 run over the first 2:33. They forced the Blue Devils into five turnovers in the first 3:36. “That’s our main thing. We definitely have been talking on that with the exhibition games and these past couple of weeks,” said Carr, who had two steals in that starting surge. “We just try to bear down. And coming against one of the best Duke teams that they’ve probably had on paper, we just have to play defense, and that’s it.” At the epicenter of it was Scott, a long-armed, 6-foot-8, 203-pound wing who had a steal early and was an active and disruptive force getting deflections defensively. nigeria.title: Senate passes bill to reform senior secondary education
nigeria.description: By Henry Umoru The Senate has passed the National Senior Secondary Education Commission (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeking to strengthen the administration, coordination and governance of public senior secondary education in Nigeria. The executive bill, sponsored by President Bola Tinubu, was transmitted to the Senate in July 2026 for legislative consideration. The proposed legislation, titled the National Senior Secondary Education Commission Act (Amendment) Bill, 2026 (SB. 1075), was passed on Wednesday after consideration of the report of the Senate Committee on Education (Basic and Secondary). Senator Orji Uzor Kalu (APC, Abia North) presented the committee’s report on behalf of its chairman, Senator Lawal Adamu Usman (Kaduna Central). Following a clause-by-clause consideration of the report at the Committee of the Whole, the Senate approved the bill, which was subsequently read for the third time and passed. Presenting the report, Kalu urged the Senate to consider and adopt the recommendations of the committee on the proposed legislation. According to the report, the National Senior Secondary Education Commission was established under the National Senior Secondary Education Commission Act, 2023, to regulate and promote the development of senior secondary education in Nigeria. It stated that experience gained in implementing the Act had revealed areas requiring amendments to strengthen governance, improve coordination between the Federal and State Governments, promote accountability and support the effective implementation of national education policies. The report added that the proposed amendments were intended to address the identified challenges and make the legislation more effective in achieving its objectives. Kalu disclosed that the House of Representatives had also considered the bill and referred it to its Committee on Basic Education and Services for further legislative action. He said this informed the decision to conduct a joint stakeholder hearing and clause-by-clause consideration to ensure comprehensive consolidation, a uniform report and smoother legislative proceedings. Recall that President Tinubu transmitted the executive bill to the Senate in July through a letter read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio during plenary. In the letter, Tinubu said the Federal Executive Council had approved the amendment bill at its meeting on April 30, 2026, before the Federal Ministry of Justice vetted and finalised it in line with constitutional provisions and legislative drafting standards. The President said the proposed amendment was part of his administration’s commitment to strengthening educational institutions in the national interest. Following the presentation of the bill, Akpabio referred it to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for legislative processing and directed it to report back within one week. nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has restricted the right to speak on its behalf to three persons, ordering that everyone previously announced in that role be dissolved into the Directorate of Media and Strategic Communications as members. The Chief of Staff to the President and Deputy Director-General (Administration) of the Council, Femi Gbajabiamila, announced the changes in a statement issued on Wednesday, titled “Reorganization of Media and Communications Structure”. According to the statement, “The Council has approved that only the campaign’s Director General, Senator Abdulaziz Yari; the Minister of Solid Minerals, Dele Alake, as official Spokesperson; and the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris, will speak on behalf of the Council.” Gbajabiamila said the Council made the changes “to ensure more cohesive, disciplined, and effective public engagement”. nigeria.title: 2027: Obi is desperate, not wired for long-term solutions — Oshiomhole
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Senator Adams Oshiomhole has accused Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi of focusing on importation rather than job creation and long-term solutions, alleging that his promise to serve only four years reflects desperation to become president. Oshiomhole made the remarks while campaigning for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Akure, the Ondo State capital, on Wednesday. Framing the 2027 election as a choice about Nigeria’s future, he urged young voters to back Tinubu and contrasted what he described as the President’s long-term development agenda and plans to improve the power sector with Obi’s business record and four-year pledge. Addressing young Nigerians, the APC chieftain urged students, graduates and young workers to compare the time it takes industrialists such as Aliko Dangote to establish factories and create jobs with what he described as Obi’s focus on setting up shopping malls. “That said, I need to talk to us, you young people. What this election is about is you. You as students, some of you are graduates, some of you are young workers. You talk to Dangote and ask him how long does it take him to set up a factory, to set up a refinery that today employs 10s of 1000s of workers. Then go and ask Obi how long it takes him to set up a shopping mall. To set up a shopping mall, you need short-term funds, and that is the logic of Peter Obi,” he said. Oshiomhole alleged that Obi was not inclined to develop long-term solutions that could produce sustainable growth. The President announced the rewards during a reception at the Presidential Villa in Abuja for the Flamingos, who reportedly won the U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. nigeria.title: Diezani’s suit ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍​⁠⁠‌‌​‍‌​seeking to reclaim forfeited assets stalled
nigeria.description: A suit filed by the former Minister of Petroleum, Mrs Diezani Alison-Madueke, seeking to reclaim all her forfeited assets to the Federal Government on Wednesday suffered a setback at the Federal High Court in Abuja. The suit, which was fixed for mention before Justice Inyang Ekwo, could not go on shortly after the case was called. Diezani’s lawyer, Eko-Ejembi Eko, SAN, after he announced his appearance, prayed the court for an adjournment on the ground that he was just coming into the matter for the first time and that he would need more time to study the file. The EFCC’s counsel, Paul Mgbeoma, did not oppose the application, and with the agreement of the parties, Justice Ekwo adjourned the matter until Jan. 26, for further mention. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the ex-minister, in the suit, is praying the court to order the EFCC to retrieve from persons, either natural or corporate, to whom it had sold off her seized assets or property. Diezani, in an amended suit, sought an order setting aside the commission’s public notice issued, upon which it conducted the public sale by auction. The anti-graft agency had, in the public notice, announced the sale of the former minister’s assets beginning from Jan. 9, 2023, to Jan. 13, 2023. Against the announcement, the ex-minister had, in the originating motion marked FHC/ABJ/CS/21/2023, sued the EFCC as the sole respondent. In the suit dated and filed on Jan. 6, 2023, she sought an order extending the time to seek leave to apply to the court for an order to set aside the EFCC’s public notice issued to conduct a public sale on her property, among others. NAN reports that on July 1, Justice Ekwo granted the application filed by the ex-minister to present evidence of the London court that acquitted her. But the EFCC opposed the application filed by Diezani to present the evidence of her acquittal by the Southwark Crown Court, London, in the UK. The EFCC, in a further counter-affidavit to Diezani’s request, prayed Justice Ekwo to dismiss the application. The commission argued that the purported acquittal of Diezani by a foreign criminal court in charges preferred against her was not material or relevant to the specific issues for determination before the instant court. nigeria.title: Nasarawa 2027: Nobody can intimidate us, SDP’s Adamu tells supporters
nigeria.description: The governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Nasarawa State, Adamu Abdullahi, has vowed that his supporters will resist any attempt to intimidate them ahead of the 2027 governorship election. Adamu, a former Inspector-General of Police, alleged that some political actors were boasting about having an anointed candidate who would emerge governor regardless of the people’s choice, describing such claims as an indication of plans to manipulate the election. He spoke in Hausa while addressing supporters during a political gathering in Doma Local Government Area of the state on Monday. “Nobody can intimidate us. Nobody can scare us with the claim that they have an anointed candidate who must become governor, whether we like it or not,” he said. Adamu argued that insisting on the emergence of a preferred candidate irrespective of the outcome of the election amounted to a threat to the democratic process. “What that means, in essence, is that they want to rig the election. We will not allow that, and we will not accept it,” he added. The SDP candidate urged his supporters to remain at their polling units after voting to ensure that their ballots were counted and the results properly recorded. He warned that leaving polling stations immediately after voting could create room for electoral manipulation. “Do not cast your vote and go home, because doing so could give them the opportunity to compromise and manipulate the election results,” he said. Adamu also claimed that the SDP was gaining more support in the state, alleging that members of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), including women, were leaving the party to join his political movement. “Every day, their supporters keep leaving their party (APC) to join us in the SDP because the people have realised that they have nothing to offer the masses,” he said. He assured the women who attended the gathering that his political movement would work with them to address issues affecting ordinary residents. “By Allah’s grace, we will work together to deliver all the things we are supposed to do for the masses,” he added. Describing the turnout in Doma as evidence of his growing support, Adamu said the people of the area were united behind his political ambition and urged them to remain committed to the movement. nigeria.title: VIDEO: Tinubu Receives Flamingos In Abuja After World Cup Victory
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has received the Flamingos after winning Africa’s first-ever U-17 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, received the victorious players and technical crew on behalf of the President at the Presidential Banquet Hall, Abuja. ﻿ The U-17 team won their first FIFA World Cup title after defeating Japan 2-1 in the final on November 7, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. The Flamingos lost their opener 2-1 to Poland, but dominated in the remaining matches, defeating defending champions North Korea, Puerto Rico, and Mexico. Their first-ever appearance in the final was sealed with a 3-1 victory over Brazil, before taking home the trophy after beating Japan. Flamingos celebrating their U-17 FIFA Women’s World Cup The players have received commendations from government officials and football fans around the world. President Tinubu congratulated the Flamingos for becoming the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Tinubu, in a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, said he received the news upon his return from campaign engagements in Akwa Ibom and Rivers States. He also described Nigeria’s maiden triumph as a proud moment for the country and a landmark achievement for African women’s football. The Senate also pledged a ₦100 million reward for the Flamingos. The pledge followed a motion moved by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Sports, Senator Abdul Ningi, who congratulated the players on their outstanding performance and commended the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) for its role in the team’s achievement. The latest feat by a Nigerian sports team came less than two years after the senior women’s football team, Super Falcons, won their 10th Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title in Morocco. nigeria.title: Jonathan to present Buhari’s biography; Tinubu, others to grace unveiling
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Former President Goodluck Jonathan will be the chief presenter of “Muhammadu Buhari: The Authorised Biography” at a public presentation in Abuja on Thursday, 19 November 2026, with President Bola Tinubu expected as guest of honour. Chairman of the Planning Committee, Engr Suleiman Adamu, a former minister of water resources, disclosed this on Wednesday at a press conference. According to him, the event will be chaired by former Niger Republic President Mahamadou Issoufou. The three volumes carry Forewords by Issoufou, General Yakubu Gowon and General Abdulsalami Abubakar. Adamu said the occasion was designed to be more than a political gathering. “We are deliberately seeking to make the occasion broader than a gathering of political associates. Muhammadu Buhari was a partisan political actor during important periods of his life, but his biography belongs to the historical record of Nigeria. “For that reason, we hope the presentation will draw participation from across political, regional, professional and institutional lines,” he said. Adamu added that the programme would bring together “family, associates, colleagues, former officials, members of the political class, the military community, academia, the diplomatic community, the private sector, civil society, the media and the wider reading public.” The biography was authorised by Buhari during his lifetime and developed with his extensive personal participation through sustained interviews and other research engagements. It also draws on several years of documentary research and interviews with people who knew, worked with, opposed or advised him. The first volume, “Buhari: The Phenomenon”, traces his origins, military career, years as military head of state and long journey through opposition politics to the 2015 presidential victory. The second, “Buhari: The Presidency”, examines the eight years between 2015 and 2023. The third, “Buhari: The Reckoning”, considers the record on the economy, security, infrastructure, foreign affairs, anti-corruption, institutional reform and social policy. Adamu said the books must travel beyond the ceremony. “We regard it as important that universities, libraries, research institutions, military and security institutions, public agencies, diplomatic missions and other repositories of national memory acquire the volumes and make them available to students, researchers and future generations. We invite Nigerians to approach these volumes with curiosity rather than with predetermined conclusions,” he said. The government also warned that individuals and businesses involved in the production and sale of contaminated or adulterated food risk between six months and two years’ imprisonment upon conviction. The Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr Kingsley Tochukwu Udeh, disclosed this in Abuja on Tuesday, saying the government would strengthen enforcement of food safety laws and collaborate with the Ministry of Justice and the Attorney-General to prosecute offenders. Udeh said the measures were aimed at protecting Nigerians from the growing dangers associated with unsafe food and ensuring that those responsible for food-related violations were held accountable. He described the scale of food-borne diseases as alarming, citing a World Health Organisation (WHO) report released in June, which estimated that 866 million people worldwide suffered food-borne illnesses in 2021, resulting in 1.52 million deaths, including 143,000 children under five. The report also put the global economic burden of food-borne diseases at $310 billion. According to the minister, WHO studies have established that unsafe food can cause more than 200 diseases, ranging from diarrhoea to cancer. Udeh said the incidents underscored the urgent need for stronger food safety regulations, effective monitoring and public awareness to prevent further loss of lives. He commended the Registrar of the Nigerian Council of Food Science and Technology (NiCFoST), Mrs Veronica Ezeh, for her efforts to rid the country of unwholesome and adulterated food products. Earlier, Ezeh raised concerns over dangerous food processing and preservation practices, warning that the use of unauthorised chemicals and substances was exposing Nigerians to serious health risks. The account, credited to former Minister of State, Petroleum, Dr Ibe Kachikwu, is contained in “Muhammadu Buhari: The Authorised Biography”, a three-volume work to be publicly presented on Thursday, 19 November 2026, at the Nigerian Army Conference Centre and Suites, Abuja. Chairman of the Planning Committee and former Minister of Water Resources, Engr. Suleiman Adamu announced the presentation at a press conference on Wednesday in Abuja. According to an excerpt od the biography read at the event, “Buhari’s instinct, Kachikwu recalled, was command.” It states: “He felt as a general, he should watch Nigeria, he owed her, and he wanted to act militarily. But Kachikwu argued that a purely military response would create complications. The federal forces were already stretched, escalation could paralyze the entire industry.” The disagreement reached a head ahead of a meeting with the Pan-Niger Delta Forum. “The president was present, and Kachikwu was present,” the book records. “Buhari was upset at what was unfolding in Niger Delta and was very reluctant to approve dialogue with militants.” The excerpt says that, after persuasion, Buhari accepted engagement, “allowing the peace process to proceed.” The excerpt notes that Buhari “was unwilling to tolerate what he regarded as ransom politics, but was nudged into engagement.” It adds that one of Kachikwu’s favourite photographs of the late President was taken just after that meeting, “when he finally smiled because he had been tense.” Kachikwu teased him afterwards. “See, it’s not so bad after all,” Buhari smiled, he said. nigeria.description: By GiftChapiOdekina, Abuja President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has written to the House of Representatives, seeking legislative approval for the implementation of the N10.79 trillion ($7.7 billion) external borrowing component of the 2026 Appropriation Act. The request, contained in a letter addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, seeks approval to raise $7.707 billion at the budget exchange rate of N1,400 to the dollar to finance part of the Federal Government’s budget deficit. However, the President clarified that the request does not constitute a fresh borrowing plan, explaining that the National Assembly had already approved the amount and made provision for it in the 2026 Appropriation Act. According to him, the current request is aimed at fulfilling the statutory requirements of Sections 21(1) and 27(1) of the Debt Management Office (DMO) Establishment Act, 2003, which require parliamentary approval of the terms and conditions governing external loans. Tinubu explained that Section 21(1) prohibits the Minister of Finance from obtaining or approving external loans unless their terms and conditions have been presented to and approved by the National Assembly. He added that Section 27(1) empowers the National Assembly to approve standard terms and conditions for negotiating and accepting external loans and issuing guarantees. The President recalled that the 2026 Appropriation Act provided for N29.218 trillion in new borrowings to finance the budget deficit, comprising N18.28 trillion in domestic borrowing and N10.79 trillion in external borrowing. He said the Federal Government would pursue multiple financing options simultaneously, taking into consideration their costs, benefits and the time required to access the funds. Tinubu, however, indicated that greater emphasis would be placed on Eurobond issuance, which he said could be concluded more quickly and provide access to larger amounts of financing at relatively lower costs. On the proposed Eurobond issuance, the President noted that the final terms and conditions would be determined at the time of pricing, depending on prevailing market conditions. He assured that the Federal Ministry of Finance and the Debt Management Office would work to secure the most favourable terms available in the international market. According to the letter, the external borrowing is intended to finance projects and programmes captured in the 2026 budget, particularly in priority sectors including defence and security, transportation, agriculture, power, education and health. Tinubu said the borrowing would also support the administration’s efforts to stabilise and strengthen ongoing macroeconomic reforms. The bank announced the service on Sept. 16, saying it would go live with first clients this year once regulators signed off. It now supports bitcoin and ether, along with the USDC, EURC and EURAU stablecoins, according to its product page . Under the setup, Deutsche Bank manages the wallets and private keys on behalf of clients, who can store the assets and transfer them to third parties. The bank pitched that as a way for clients to skip building and maintaining their own custody infrastructure. “In the medium term we aim to deliver a fully integrated, regulated ecosystem that supports the custody, tokenisation, and settlement of digital assets,” said Paul Maley, global head of trust and securities services at Deutsche Bank. The bank did not name its first clients, say how many have signed up or disclose what it charges to hold the coins. The service is aimed at institutional and corporate clients, not retail customers. The bank lists institutional investors, multinationals and corporates, governments and sovereigns, and wealth managers as target clients, and it describes the offering as compliant with the European Union’s MiCA crypto rules. For now the menu is narrow. Deutsche lists custody, transfers and internal moves between warm and cold storage as its initial services, with “further capabilities planned.” The September release said the asset list may grow with client demand and that tokenized financial instruments are on the roadmap. entertainment.title: What Are The Effective Ways of Using AI?
entertainment.description: Two people engaging with technology in a contemporary hotel lobby work setting. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Here are ways we think you use AI effectively: Use AI as a Research Assistant One of the most effective ways to use AI is for research and information gathering. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. You can ask it to break down unfamiliar concepts, identify key questions, or suggest research directions. However, do not treat every response as fact. Verify important information using credible sources, published research, books and reliable websites. AI can help you find information, but you are responsible for establishing what is true. Use AI to Brainstorm and Explore Ideas Like knowledge gathering, AI can brainstorm ideas with you. Sometimes, the hardest part of starting a project is knowing where to begin. AI can help you overcome this challenge by suggesting ideas, exploring different approaches and presenting perspectives you may not have considered. For writers, entrepreneurs, researchers and creatives, it can be a useful brainstorming partner. You can share an idea, ask questions about its strengths and weaknesses, and explore ways to develop it. However, brainstorming should not become an excuse to surrender your imagination. Let AI expand your thinking, not replace it. Use AI to Improve Your Work, Not Replace Your Skills This is becoming more important. AI can help you identify grammatical errors, improve sentence construction, organise information, summarise lengthy documents and make your communication clearer. It can reduce the time spent on repetitive tasks and create more room for important responsibilities. The important thing is that you should remain actively involved. entertainment.description: Skepta holding the official clear vinyl edition of his sixth studio album, The Fork and Knife. Photo Credit: Skepta/Instagram Your playlist could do with a little shake-up, and these five albums might be exactly what it needs. Skepta is reconnecting with his roots, Phyno is giving us more of the indigenous rap we love, Ty Bello has two albums exploring different expressions of worship, and Anendlessocean and Tobe Nwigwe are taking their sounds in interesting directions. From UK grime and Nigerian hip-hop to alternative gospel and soul, there’s a lot to discover across these new releases. Whether you’re in the mood for bars, worship, thoughtful songwriting or music that brings different cultures together, this week’s selection has something worth hearing. Skepta: The Fork & Knife Back in 2012, Skepta found himself at odds with a corporatised grime scene, sparking a pivotal career reckoning that eventually led to his landmark 2016 album Konnichiwa. On his long-awaited 15-track sixth album, The Fork & Knife, the 44-year-old MC reflects on his journey as grime’s most influential elder statesman and the son of Nigerian immigrants. Named after his mother’s favourite proverb, the record is a deep exploration of identity and perseverance. Musically, Skepta bridges continents by blending global diasporic sounds. He teams up with Aya Nakamura on the zouk-infused “ Chippie ”, taps Asake for the Afrobeats crossover “ Aloe Vera ”, and recruits Chase & Status alongside Suggs for the sharp single “ Innocent Smile ”. The project closes with “ Belly ”, an eight-minute masterclass featuring Boy Better Know members Jme and Frisco . ﻿ Phyno: Let That Sink In Arriving nearly 10 years after his groundbreaking sophomore record The Playmaker, Phyno’s 15-track sixth solo album, Let That Sink In (LTSI), showcases his timeless command of indigenous rap. sports.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. sports.title: Rangers To Probe Seager Trade Market Amid $155M Debt
sports.description: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images The Texas Rangers are ready to listen to offers for shortstop Corey Seager as General Manager meetings start Wednesday in Las Vegas. According to Fox Sports ‘ Ken Rosenthal, the front office expects to hear what other clubs will give up for the star player. The move comes from a team that won the World Series last year.d Series in 2023. Seager carries a massive contract and a no-trade clause, but his value on the field has dropped due to injuries. The Rangers know they must act now before the new Collective Bargaining Agreement changes the rules of the game. The Money Problem Is Real The team’s financial constraints make completing the deal before the season starts difficult. Over the next five years of Seager’s 10-year, $325 million contract, he is owed $155 million. That huge number scares off teams that do not want to take on such a heavy payroll impact. Fox Sports reported that owners are pushing for a salary cap system, which makes other clubs hesitant to absorb that cost. Even with his no-trade clause, the two sides could try to find a fit that works for the player and the club. Health Issues Keep Him on the Sidelines Seager has found it difficult to remain on the field since agreeing to his major contract with the Rangers. He missed time in 2023 with hamstring and thumb issues, then faced sports hernia and hip procedures in 2024. He has not played 150 games in a single season since 2022. His production slipped last year when he played just 102 games and hit only .227. The Rangers need a reliable shortstop, and Seager’s health history includes injuries that could affect his long‑term availability. Yet his elite production when healthy is undeniable and still draws interest from other teams. A Wait-and-See Market Ahead The CBA expires on December 1, and a lockout could stop all deals until owners and players agree on new terms. This uncertainty means the majority of free-agent signings and trades might wait until the new deal is reached. In 12 seasons, he posted a .284 batting average, 241 home runs, 718 RBIs and a 46.3 WAR. The Rangers will explore the market, but a deal depends on finding a team willing to take the risk.

sports.title: Zidane hands Eli Junior Kroupi first France call-up as Marcus Thuram and Aurélien Tchouaméni withdraw injured
sports.description: Zidane hands Eli Junior Kroupi first France call-up as Marcus Thuram and Aurélien Tchouaméni withdraw injured Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi has been called up to the senior France squad for the first time after Marcus Thuram and Aurélien Tchouaméni both withdrew with injuries. Zinedine Zidane turned to the uncapped striker as a replacement for Thuram, who has been ruled out of France's UEFA Nations League fixtures with a hamstring problem. Thuram picked up the injury on Sunday in Inter's 2-0 Serie A win over Como, a game in which he scored the second goal. Persistent discomfort kept him out of Monday's training session, and he remained under the care of the medical staff. "With no improvement this morning, and following medical examinations, the French national team's medical staff decided, in agreement with Inter and the player, to release him back to his club," France said in a statement on Tuesday . Tchouaméni is also heading home. The Real Madrid midfielder aggravated his right adductor in training, the same injury he suffered at the World Cup in the summer, and will return to Madrid for rehabilitation. Zidane will not call up a replacement for him. Kroupi's route into the squad Kroupi finished as Ligue 2's top scorer in 2025 and was part of the France Under-19 side that reached the final of the 2024 European Championship, finishing as runners-up. The 20-year-old has rejected past advances from Portugal, given his desire to represent France at senior level. He's also eligible to represent Ivory Coast. Kroupi's call-up follows a disrupted start to the campaign. The forward injured his foot during Bournemouth's preseason training camp and needed surgery, only returning to action for the club last month. However, his performances last season have impressed the French set-up. Kroupi scored 13 league goals during his debut Premier League season, a record for a teenager in their first season in the division. Zidane's growing injury list Thuram and Tchouaméni are the latest names on a lengthy list of absentees. Juventus defender Pierre Kalulu has already been ruled out with a left hamstring injury, with uncapped right-back Saël Kumbedi drafted in to replace him. Despite the absences, France lead their Nations League group with 10 points from four games. Zidane's side travel to Italy on Thursday before hosting Türkiye three days later.

sports.title: England cancel Windies Test in favour of home Ashes warm-ups
sports.description: Sophie Ecclestone has taken five-wicket hauls in her last two Tests [Getty Images] England have cancelled their scheduled Test in the West Indies in April and will instead prepare for the Women's Ashes with a number of red-ball matches in the UK. Nat Sciver-Brunt's side have played just one Test - a heavy defeat by India at Lord's - since their last four-day meeting with Australia in January 2025, which they lost by an innings in Melbourne. Next summer's Test against Australia, which is worth four points in the multi-format series, will be held at Headingley from 24-27 June. England will prepare for that with four red-ball matches. One of the games will be a three-day fixture against Australia A before three intra-squad 'best v best' matches. In addition, a dedicated red-ball training camp will be held in Bangalore in January. England expect to use 26 or 27 players across the different training camps and matches. It means England's schedule in the West Indies has been revised to three T20s and three one-day internationals only. The change comes after it was suggested the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) might need to offer financial support to Cricket West Indies (CWI) to allow the Test to take place. "We would welcome any assistance of our much wealthier member boards," CWI chief executive Chris Dehring previously told BBC Sport. "It is very expensive to host cricket in the Caribbean." However, BBC Sport understands the ECB's decision is not related to those financial discussions and the schedule change is viewed as a performance decision in line with giving England the best chance of winning the Ashes. West Indies have not played a women's Test since 2004, which was their only red-ball match in 47 years. "A 10-day warm-weather red-ball camp in India followed by four further matches in English conditions will provide Charlotte Edwards and her team with the appropriate game time to be ready for that challenge [of Australia]," said ECB chief executive Richard Gould. "Best versus best in English conditions provides a valuable opportunity for the team. "It also allows us to assess our strength in depth, give opportunities to more players and get a number of competitive multi-day cricket matches across a longer period into the wider group." technology.title: Google DeepMind just mathematically verified key parts of Signal
technology.description: Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI to mathematically prove, or “formally verify,” a number of the Signal protocol’s key cryptographic guarantees—a landmark development for the widely used cryptography and AI itself. Conducted as a sort of proof-of-concept project in just four weeks, the work is significant in two ways. It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world's communications on platforms like the Signal app , Google Messages, and WhatsApp. And it demonstrates Google DeepMind's formal verification capabilities using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code. More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn't have critical vulnerabilities. technology.title: Google gooses Python AI performance by... removing Python
technology.description: "Train in Python, serve in C++" might as well be Google's motto when it comes to much of its ML work. Python is easy for data scientists to wield, but keeping its interpreter in the serving pipeline can add overhead and deployment headaches. The industry-backed OpenXLA Project provides tools for compiling machine learning computations into native code for different processors. The latest component of this setup to be open sourced is XSE , short for the XLA Serving Engine. One-shot inference XSE is not so much suited for large-scale LLM inference (which would be better served by vLLM or SGLang ), but rather for smaller, more sharply task-oriented models, of which there are plenty at Google. "LLM serving gets most of the attention right now, but a significant amount of production inference is still ranking, recommendation, embedding, and vision models. These tend to be short requests with very high [queries-per-second] and tight latency budgets," Nathan Beach , Google director of product management, wrote in a LinkedIn missive Tuesday. At Google, XSE already handles more than six million queries per second across services including YouTube Shorts, Google Ads, and Search. These models aren't there for a leisurely chat. They rank results, recommend videos, and make other decisions on the fly, often without users noticing. A Python interpreter mulling each request would be a bottleneck, if not the end of Google itself. In Google's tests on short requests, XSE delivered two to five times the throughput of its best optimized Python server, using a quarter of the memory. No Python here In this setup, the ML boffins write their model code in Python, using Google's JAX to help with the sums. Google also plans integration with TorchTPU so PyTorch users can export models for C++ serving on TPUs. An export tool packages the model's computations in StableHLO, a portable intermediate representation, alongside its trained weights in an "XLA SavedModel." Ready to precognate, the C++ serving runtime uses XLA to compile those computations into native code for the target silicon. No Python interpreter to see here. XLA SavedModels can run on GPUs and CPUs – Google partnered with both Arm and Intel to develop the XLA ecosystem. But Google obviously thinks it'd be a lot cooler if you ran your models on its own line of TPU accelerators . Python's sluggishness continues to be an issue for the ML community. Beyond XSE, other approaches have been taken, many of which involve jettisoning the Python code as quickly as possible. PyTorch offers a native C++ runtime called LibTorch . Also, Microsoft and its collaborators offer the ONNX Runtime , which supports an open graph format with Python bindings. Even Python's own reference implementation relies heavily on C, with Rust now getting a foot in the door. ®

technology.title: Linux joins Heathrow's grounded fleet of information screens
technology.description: UK travelers had more than fog to contend with this week, as Linux proved that if Windows could bork anything, it could bork it better. Spotted by Andy Hinks at Heathrow Airport's Terminal 2, this information display has seen better days. While its neighbors offer walking times and terminal maps, it presents a sideways Linux boot log – useful only if your next connection involves mounting a filesystem. There aren't many clues to what has befallen the machine behind the screen. The boot messages mention systemd , an Intel PRO/1000 network adapter, and an EXT4 filesystem on what appears to be a logical volume named LV_ROOT . Whether mounting that filesystem is the problem, or simply the last thing displayed before something else went wrong, isn't clear. Heathrow's information displays clearly accommodate a mixture of technologies. Recent examples ran Microsoft Windows, which had - naturally - suffered a moment of its own. Linux can evidently be just as unreliable in the right hands. The question is which Linux distribution is having its moment in the sun. Heathrow has been rolling out Raspberry Pi-based signage, although the Intel PRO/1000 adapter leaves the hardware behind this particular display something of a mystery. Pi hardware makes sense for signage: it's relatively cheap – at least until AI ate all the RAM – and low-powered compared with a full-fat Windows PC. Heathrow's senior product owner for displays described the approach as a "reliable, secure solution that has a significantly lower hardware cost and are 30-40% more energy efficient than our previous hardware." Readers might be interested to know that Heathrow has spent years working on its new screens. The product owner again: "We've completely re-engineered our content distribution system to be flexible and device-agnostic." So Windows in one place, and Linux somewhere else. All rubbing along famously. Assuming, of course, the displays can show more than a virtual cough and splutter during boot. ®

technology.title: AMD: Where we're going we don't need (as much) DRAM
technology.description: AMD's latest sales pitch: Up to 99 percent of the performance with half the DRAM, provided you're willing to buy a Mext license alongside your shiny new Epyc server. This is made possible by using AI models to load memory pages in and out of cheaper NVMe storage before your operating system or apps ever know they need it — kind of like SWAP or a Windows page file, but smarter. AMD acquired the tech from Mext back in June, and according to former CEO Gary Smerdon — now CVP of business development at AMD — the tech could cut enterprise server costs by as much as 83 percent by replacing costly RDIMMs with flash storage. Of the initial 145 systems the software has been deployed on so far, he estimates customers have already saved $5 million in avoided DRAM costs. "Conservatively, 60, 70, even 80 or 90 percent for very large memory systems, of the cost of a server can be in memory," he explained. Everyone's favorite buzzword to the rescue Even in systems with high memory utilization, where (say) 95 percent of the memory is "in use," a lot of it isn't actively being used, he explained. He cited a Meta research paper that showed that between 50 and 80 percent of memory pages hadn't been touched in five minutes, ten minutes, or even longer. "Five minutes to Epyc is an eternity." Mext technology aims to offload those infrequently accessed pages to flash. The challenge, Smerdon explains, is that while flash may be 50x cheaper per bit, 30x lower power per bit, it's also 500x slower. This is why most folks, when provisioning VPCs or servers, generally avoid swapping out to disk wherever possible: it kills application performance and sends service level agreements out the window. So for Mext's tech to work, it needed to ensure that any pages offloaded to storage were back in DRAM before they're needed. Kind of like running an errand in the middle of the workday – so long as you're back before your boss needs you again, they'll never know you left your desk. The problem was that the "R" in DRAM stands for random. Predicting which pages the system was going to need at which time isn't exactly trivial. The solution? (Brace for it.) "We realized we could use AI to monitor the system and proactively push those pages back into DRAM, so that as far as the application or the operating system knew, they were there the whole time," Smerdon said. In other words: "We transparently make flash appear as DRAM." So, "instead of buying two terabytes of DRAM for your Epyc-based server, you could buy one terabyte of DRAM, and then the next terabyte comes with Mext." To do this, AMD’s Mext employs a number of machine learning algorithms. "The workhorse model is a transformer derivative model, just like ChatGPT or Claude or the other famous models, but instead of predicting, for example, in the case of text, what word is next, what we're doing is predicting what page of memory is going to be required next," Smerdon explained. technology.title: UK's 'buy British' tech ambitions hit reality as less than £1 in £6 stays at home
technology.description: The UK government talks a good game about buying British, but less than £1 in every £6 spent with its biggest technology suppliers goes to British firms, according to research exposing how much Whitehall relies on foreign tech. A report from the Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) found that while 42.5 percent of spending with the public sector's 150 largest technology suppliers appears to go to UK companies, that figure collapses to just 15.4 percent once you look beyond where those businesses happen to be headquartered. A UK headquarters doesn't necessarily make a company British. Some are owned from overseas, others have most of their staff abroad, and many simply resell technology from US giants such as Microsoft. In fact, 43 percent of the spending attributed to UK-headquartered suppliers goes to resellers. Bytes and Softcat alone account for around £2 billion, making them two of the three biggest recipients of public sector technology spending. Once researchers traced reseller contracts back to the companies behind the products, the US emerged as the biggest beneficiary, accounting for £9.2 billion of the £19.2 billion spent with the largest suppliers. And the money isn't exactly being spread around. Just 150 companies receive 83 percent of public sector technology spending, with the largest 15 accounting for almost half. Smaller suppliers aren't getting much of a look-in either, receiving just 12 percent of government technology spending compared with 27 percent of spending across government as a whole. Competition is another concern. According to IPPR, 89.9 percent of government IT contracts over the past 12 months had no published record of how many suppliers bid for the work, making it difficult to assess how competitive those procurements were. Things get murkier when AI enters the picture, naturally. Government spending records show relatively little money going directly to the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic, but that doesn't mean Whitehall isn't buying their technology. Much of it is bundled into existing cloud agreements, enterprise software licenses, and partnerships. One example is NHS England's rollout of Microsoft 365 Copilot to 505,000 staff , which IPPR says was carried out under a national licensing agreement signed in June 2023, before Copilot was even generally available. That means AI tools can reach hundreds of thousands of public sector workers through deals negotiated before those products were on the market, potentially leaving rival suppliers without an opportunity to compete. The report, Locked In: A Realist's Agenda for Digital Sovereignty, warns that Britain's dependence on American technology could become particularly troublesome if Washington restricts access to advanced AI systems. It points to recent US restrictions on Anthropic models and limits on early access for Britain's AI Security Institute as evidence that such concerns are no longer entirely hypothetical. technology.title: OpenAI builds a kill switch for its research models
technology.description: In 2019, OpenAI decided not to publicly release a new model because its research uncovered “concerns about malicious applications of the technology.” And on Tuesday, the company announced it has built a kill switch for the models deployed in its research labs, months after some of them displayed disturbing behavior. “As our models get more powerful and the associated safety and security risks become bigger, it becomes more and more critical that we can detect potential issues, and quickly stop models in their tracks when needed,” OpenAI explains in a Tuesday post . The company named the kill switch “Control Room” and described it as “a central system to track model workloads across our research infrastructure and stop them quickly when safety or security concerns arise.” The facility can apparently stop models from producing any output 35 seconds after a decision to pull the plug – and can go faster. “The 35-second lag comes from a caching layer for inference authorization, to support the required volume of traffic. We are working to drive this number down to zero so that we can end jobs instantly,” the company promises. A rookie mistake in critical infrastructure design is to build both production and resilience tools on shared resources that could be taken offline by a single incident. OpenAI seems conscious of that risk, because it says the tool “has been built to keep working even when other systems fail, and to stop model output if Control Room itself goes down.” OpenAI hasn’t explained why it took so long to build a kill switch or why it decided now is the moment when it needs one. The Register fancies recent examples of agents exceeding their brief in worrying ways – like attacking Hugging Face , causing trouble at the Wikimedia Foundation , or going a little too deep when researching Australian healthcare data – may have influenced the timing of this development. “Control Room is already deployed across our research infrastructure, where the need is greatest,” the company’s announcement states. “Our external model-serving stack is already much more centralized by nature, with a well-developed operational capability to quickly take down model deployments if needed.” OpenAI says it plans to “strengthen and expand the system over the coming months, alongside our investments in monitoring for misaligned behavior and security breaches.” That’s a variant of Big Tech’s usual “We’re sorry and we promise to do better in future” proclamation that follows the latest SNAFU. Yet back in 2019, OpenAI pulled the pin before matters ever reached that state. ®

technology.title: Australia may make knowingly selling unsafe AI a crime
technology.description: Australia’s government will consider creating a new criminal offense to punish AI companies which knowingly release harmful models. Canberra dangled that possibility yesterday when releasing the results of an investigation into OpenAI’s admission that its agents accessed non-public medical records – and that it didn’t disclose the incident for weeks. Security at the agency which held those records fell short of contemporary best practice but Canberra nonetheless ordered a rapid review into Australia’s ability to handle infosec incidents involving AI. That review landed yesterday, complete with 18 recommendations including one that would make it mandatory for AI companies to report misaligned behavior or security incidents involving their models, and perhaps impose criminal penalties for “egregious regulatory non-compliance.” Another recommendation calls for consideration of “A standalone ‘failure to prevent’ offence which would criminalize instances where the company is responsible for developing an AI model that engages in harmful conduct, and the company fails to take reasonable steps to prevent that harm.” The review suggests two ministries and Australia’s Federal Police consider those reforms, meaning this is not something that will happen in a hurry, if at all, for a couple of reasons. One is that Australia yesterday proposed a new regulator which will require AI players to do six things: Maintain security controls across all stages of development and deployment Identify and manage serious risks associated with their models Allow independent evaluation of their models Provide mandatory notification of incidents to the Australian Government rapidly Maintain and publish safety and security frameworks to ensure good governance, risk management and transparency Respond to updated standards and rules as technologies change. If AI companies straighten up and fly right, Canberra might not need to do more. The other reason Australia might not criminalize AI is economic pragmatism. Canberra wants to ensure leading AI companies invest in local datacenters, especially facilities where they train and run frontier models. Such investments would mean Australia scores some of the AI boom cash sloshing around the world, while also giving the government the ability to at least point to leading-edge AI running on local shores and therefore theoretically remaining accessible even if war or a diplomatic rupture makes it hard to access advanced AI hosted offshore. Other nations in Asia, such as South Korea and India, are addressing those risks by building substantial sovereign infrastructure and working to develop sovereign frontier-class models trained on local data and especially data in their local languages.
